newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-ASC has photo of rogue TNT investor.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-ASC has photo of rogue TNT investor.

text.p: The Australian Securities Commission (ASC) said on Friday it had a photograph of the man known as Mark Booth whose profits from trading in TNT Ltd call options has been frozen by court order.

"Enquiries so far suggest that the name "Mark Booth" is an alias. A consistent description of him has been given by witnesses interviewed, and photographic evidence obtained from a bank security video," the ASC said.
It said the Federal Court continued the freeze on Booth's profits from trading in TNT options until February 7 next year.

An ASC spokeswoman also said the regulator had interviewed staff at TNT and its likely new parent, Koninklijke PTT Nederland (KPN) about takeover negotiations between the two express freight companies.
KPN annnounced an agreed A$2.0 billion bid for TNT on October 2.
"The ASC is continuing its investigations of a number of persons who traded in options prior to the announcement of the proposed takeover by KPN," it said in a statement.
"TNT and KPN have co-operated with the ASC's enquiries and have provided the names of over 100 people who participated in the takeover negotiations," the ASC said.
"The large number of people involved has added to the complexity of this investigation."

Before Friday's statement, the ASC investigation was believed to only involve trading by Booth through the brokerage firm Ord Minnett and two other options deals handled by Macquarie Equities which were of less concern to the regulator.

"The ASC has been using a wide range of investigative techniques in order to identify and locate Mr Booth. A Federal Agent and intelligence specialist have been attached to the investigation team," the ASC said.
It said Booth's profits of about A$2.0 million from the options trade had been frozen in an Ord Minnett cash management account.

Booth spent A$90,000 in September to buy TNT call options which had a strike price of A$2.00, well above the ruling TNT share price and "out of the money" until KPN launched its A$2.45 per share bid. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
